title: Freya and the Cipher Again
premise: Juniper Pemberton, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of her family in row twelve, is approached by a stranger claiming she once saved his life—a favor she has no memory of—and that the debt must now be repaid: he needs her expertise to decode flight data implicating three governments in a cover-up of deliberate sabotage. As Juniper digs into the cipher hidden in the black-box transcript, she uncovers evidence that row twelve was targeted, and an assassin begins eliminating everyone who touches the file. Hunted across borders with a ragtag found family of whistleblowers, Juniper must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the only people she has left, ending with her broadcasting the decoded data at devastating personal cost—surviving, but never again invisible.
about_author: Felix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a coastal cabin, drawing on real investigative procedure and the quiet griefs of those left behind.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Two years after losing her family in row twelve, Juniper survives on caffeine and insomnia until a stranger named Elias Voss appears at her door, insisting she once pulled him from a burning wreck—a crash she has no record of investigating. He leaves a flash drive and a warning: 'They know you're looking.' The emotional beat is disorientation; her carefully managed invisibility cracks for the first time.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Unable to resist, Juniper runs the flash drive through her old agency tools and finds encrypted flight-data anomalies from her family's crash—impossible control inputs, then a scrubbed log. When she requests the original files, her access is revoked within the hour. The beat is dread deepening into resolve: this wasn't an accident, and someone is watching her in real time.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals the truth he can prove: he was a courier for a covert consortium, and the 'favor' was a fabricated memory implanted to create leverage over Juniper. He offers her a choice—walk away or help him decrypt the full manifest of sabotaged flights. The beat is betrayal and moral vertigo; Juniper realizes her grief has been weaponized, yet the data is real.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Working from a safehouse, Juniper and Elias map the cipher to a shared surveillance program spanning three nations, each laundering blame onto the others. A contact inside the air safety board agrees to verify the findings—then misses their meeting. The beat is mounting paranoia as allies become liabilities and the conspiracy's scale eclipses anything Juniper imagined.

chapters.title: The Man Who Erases Crashes
chapters.summary: Assassin Marek's POV. Introduced coldly efficient, Marek eliminates the board contact and studies Juniper's file, noting with professional curiosity that she was supposed to die in row twelve too. He reports to his handler that the investigator is still breathing. The beat is chilling menace—the reader sees the machinery of erasure turning toward Juniper before she does.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the run, Juniper gathers unlikely allies: a disgraced journalist, a hacker who lost her brother to one of the sabotaged flights, and Elias himself, whose guilt becomes fierce loyalty. In a cramped Rotterdam apartment they crack the cipher's final layer together. The beat is warmth amid danger—Juniper feels, for the first time since row twelve, that she belongs to something living.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Buried
chapters.summary: Hacker Nadia's POV. The decrypted archive reveals not just sabotage but a ledger: governments sold 'deniable disasters' to corporate clients, and row twelve was purchased by a defense contractor silencing a whistleblower seated in 12C. The beat is fury and heartbreak—Juniper learns her family died as a line item, and that the buyer sits on the oversight committee meant to prevent it.

chapters.title: Running Out of Sky
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With the committee convening in Geneva in seventy-two hours to bury the evidence permanently, the group plans to broadcast the archive during the session. But Marek closes in: a decoy safehouse burns, Elias takes a bullet covering their escape, and Nadia is captured. The beat is desperation and sacrifice—the price of survival comes due, and Juniper must decide what she's willing to trade.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (climax). Posing as a delegate's aide, Juniper infiltrates the Geneva session while Elias, wounded, holds off Marek in the building's service corridors. Juniper hijacks the chamber's feed and plays the ledger aloud as delegates scramble; Marek reaches her at the console but hesitates when she names his own sister's flight from the list. The beat is cathartic confrontation—truth spoken at gunpoint, corruption exposed mid-lie.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (resolution). Weeks later, inquiries open in two countries; the contractor's executives are indicted, though the deepest architects slip away, and Marek vanishes—leaving Juniper a single message: 'Debt cleared.' Elias recovers; Nadia is freed in a prisoner exchange. Juniper sleeps through the night for the first time in two years, then wakes and starts writing everything down. The beat is bittersweet peace: survival cost everything except the truth, and the truth was enough.
